gap: No result ChatGPT got states what an RV inverter really draws with nothing plugged in. One named owner, staldor, measured 10.0 W at 12 V with no load on a Victron Phoenix 12/1200 rated at 7 W, which is about 240 Wh a day. Renogy rates the 2000W UPS inverter that ChatGPT recommended at under 18 W idle, which works out to as much as 432 Wh a day, about a third of a 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery (1,280 Wh).
standout_why: I compared against the cited Victron article 'How to Size a Solar System for Your RV' (2026-05-04). Its only inverter figure is a planning allowance of 'about 10-15% extra' for AC loads, with no idle draw, efficiency or measured data. I could not compare the cited Renogy 'RV Inverter Installation Guide' properly because WebFetch returned only its navigation (6,855 characters) and the article body did not load. I could not open rvtime.com at all because of an SSL certificate error. ChatGPT's answer gives sizes and prices only. It shows no idle-draw figure and no measured result for any of the three Renogy cards.
decides: It doesn't change the size recommendation, but it does change which inverter to buy for boondocking. Idle draw adds up every hour the inverter is left on. At the 18 W rating, the Renogy 2000W UPS unit could use about 34% of a 100Ah lithium battery a day doing nothing. That points toward a model with an ECO/search mode, or a smaller inverter for overnight loads. In 4WDing Australia's long-term test, Aaron Schubert reported that the Renogy 2000W UPS unit smelled of 'warm, smoky electronics' after about 10 minutes at 1,200 W. That is only 60% of its rating, so it argues against relying on the 2000W model for a 1,000–1,300 W microwave or induction cooktop. It favors the 3000W size ChatGPT suggested for larger appliances.

findings.note: Aaron Schubert, 4WDing Australia. Published 2022-12-24, updated 2024-04-08. This was real-world use in a ute canopy (2000W) and a camper (3000W UPS model), not a lab test. He measured no temperature, idle draw or efficiency. The 1,200 W load was an induction cooktop, which is 60% of the 2000W rating. The article says these are the UPS-function inverters, not the inverter-chargers. It does not give a regional model number, so it may not be the exact US PUH unit.
